items.text: The Hold hand has its own animation, like the waves off the finger's tip: while Hold is on, the line across the fist vibrates and short dashes radiate out from it to the left and right. Reduced-motion settings get still dashes.

iPhone upright: the grid now sizes itself to what is left of the screen, in play and in edit, so the whole thing (grid, colour and shape strip, bottom bar) fits on one screen. In edit the grid shrinks to make room for the strip.

iPhone upright: the empty gap between the grid and the bottom bar is gone. The bar sits right under the grid again and fits on the screen. In edit, the colour and shape strip now takes its room from the grid instead of pushing the bar down.

The stopwatch on the rail opens the Performance display again (it had slipped to Statistics when that was added). Holding the field pole now opens Dice and air, where the field's controls live, instead of MIDI. Every way into the display now finds its pane by name, so adding a pane cannot shift them again.

The heads-up display pop-up now sits exactly on the bottom edge of the stage and never rises above the stage's top, so its top is no longer cut off on an iPad in landscape. Its tab bar stays fixed at the bottom of the pop-up, and the panes scroll above it.
The lit one of Halo and Draw now looks like the other rail buttons: a yellow icon and a yellow bar on its left edge, with no filled yellow background. The other icon stays grey.
The Sound load button on the right edge now has the same rounded shape as its frame (top right and bottom right). Pressing it used to flash an older shape with only the bottom right rounded.

Halo and Draw are two icons stacked on the rail, Halo on top and Draw (a drop, a triangle and a circle) below, sharing one pill like a toggle group. The one in use is filled; the other is dim. Picking a colour or mark in the strip still switches Draw on.
